title: Investigate and fix ingestion bucket drift causing sparse dashboard tiles and trace-window misjoins
creator: Marco Nguyen
description: Customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported missing dashboard tiles and traces that failed to stitch during two high-traffic incidents. Investigation shows an intermittent drift between ingestion bucket boundaries and the trace-windowing service: events were landing in adjacent time buckets that the dashboard live query layer treats as out-of-range, and span stitching relied on a stale watermark that had not advanced for small shards. This ticket captures the triage, short-term mitigations applied, root-cause fix, rollout plan, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
symptoms_observed: Dashboard live panels returning empty sets for metrics that exist in raw logs
Trace views missing spans or showing disconnected child spans
Alerts for metric tile-card error rates spiking with no corresponding ingestion error logs
Incidents predominantly during burst ingress and at autoscaling boundaries
timeline_summary: 2026-02-15 03:12 UTC - Customer report: missing metrics and gaps in traces
2026-02-15 03:25 UTC - Initial mitigation: enabled high-fidelity sampling and increased trace resharding frequency
2026-02-15 04:10 UTC - Hotfix deployed (increased watermark sync frequency for affected shards)
2026-02-16 to 2026-02-20 - Continued regression testing in staging with synthetic burst traffic
2026-02-22 - Reproduced bucket drift with a latency spike on the ingest-router during autoscale events
2026-03-01 - Final code change merged to align bucket assignment logic and advance watermark atomically
root_cause: A race between the ingest-router's bucket assignment and the background compaction/ttl worker. During brief autoscale-induced reparenting, some events were assigned to a transient bucket ID that the query-time windowing code did not recognize, combined with a watermark advancement bug where small shards failed to update their last-seen timestamp, preventing KV-cache resync and span stitching.
short_term_mitigations: Force-refresh of dashboard cache for impacted tenants (applied per-tenant via admin console)
Increased shard watermark sync to 15s from 60s for the critical ingest path (temporary)
Scoped rollout of increased sampling to ensure trace continuity while fixing stitch logic
long_term_fix_plan: 1) Update ingest-router to perform bucket assignment deterministically using monotonic sequence IDs and avoid transient bucket ids
2) Make watermark advancement atomic with bucket commit so queries never observe partial state
3) Add defensive query-time rehydration: when a live-panel query sees a small time gap, auto-fetch adjacent buckets and stitch client-side
4) Add unit/integration tests with autoscale churn and burst load to validate boundary conditions
5) Backfill script to reconcile historical buckets for customers that reported gaps
deploy_plan: Canary to 5% of Hosted customers during off-peak window (03:00-06:00 UTC)
Monitor live-panel empty-tile rate, trace stitch success rate, and ingest-router error rates in real time
If canary stable for 24h, ramp to 50% then 100% with automated rollback triggers
Dedicated customers will receive coordinated upgrades with a config flag to opt-in before enforcement
monitoring_and_slo_checks: Increase alert sensitivity for tile-empty-rate (>= 2x baseline) during rollout
Add synthetic end-to-end trace stitch test every 1m for each region
Dashboard showing watermark lag per shard and bucket-assignment mismatch count
postmortem_actions: Create runbook section: 'bucket-drift detection' with remediation commands
Schedule quarterly chaos tests that simulate autoscale and resharding churn
Add telemetry to ingest-router for transient bucket assignments and expose via console
Customer outreach: personalized incident summary for impacted tenants with remediation performed and monitoring links
